qualifying_findings.title: ash_ai prompt, tool-loop, and MCP origin validation vulnerabilities
qualifying_findings.summary: ash_ai before 1.0.0 received three public CVEs: prompt text built from user input could be evaluated as EEx and execute arbitrary Elixir code; prompt-injected or malformed tool-call output could keep the tool loop recursing and resend model requests; and default MCP origin validation could be bypassed through DNS rebinding because Host and x-forwarded-proto were trusted in the decision path.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary CVE records with project security advisory references
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: ash_ai from 0.1.0 before 1.0.0 for prompt RCE; from 0.6.0 before 1.0.0 for tool-loop infinite requests; from 0.8.0 before 1.0.0 for MCP origin validation
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: The cluster joins model output, prompt templating, tool loops, and browser-origin trust into direct server-side execution and local MCP cross-site request risks.

upstream_routing.ai_wiki: ash_ai as a broad framework/entity belongs upstream if a durable entity page is needed.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General Ash/AshAI development workflow implications belong upstream; this repo keeps the security boundary.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence for in-window qualification from NVD published timestamps and linked GitHub Security Advisories.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, split prompt RCE, tool-loop exhaustion, and MCP origin validation into separate durable security leaves if they need independent maintenance.
Recheck whether ash_ai 1.0.0 is the first fixed release across Hex, OSV, and GitHub advisory metadata.

qualifying_findings.title: Eclipse Theia AI Agent Mode path traversal outside workspace
qualifying_findings.summary: Eclipse Theia 1.73.0 through versions before 1.75.0 allowed AI Agent Mode file-change tools to resolve model-supplied paths without workspace containment. Crafted relative, absolute, or home-expanded paths could write or delete files outside the workspace, and indirect prompt injection could steer the model output toward host-executed files such as shell startup files or authorized_keys.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary CVE record with Eclipse/GitHub fix references
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: This is a direct coding-agent approval and filesystem containment failure where model-generated paths can cross the workspace boundary without a confirmation dialog.

upstream_routing.ai_wiki: Theia as a developer tool/entity belongs upstream.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General AI coding-agent workflow guidance belongs upstream; workspace containment and prompt-injection write impact stay local.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence for in-window qualification from NVD and Eclipse CNA metadata.
follow_up_actions: Compare with existing coding-agent command and filesystem boundary leaves before creating a new local page.
Verify patched release notes for Theia 1.75.0 during ingest.

qualifying_findings.title: MCPHub multi-CVE authorization, SSRF, prompt, and process-spawn cluster
qualifying_findings.summary: MCPHub disclosed a cluster of in-window CVEs covering MCPB ZIP path traversal and cleanup path deletion, missing admin checks on system configuration, global prompt/resource shadowing by non-admins, bearer-key scope expansion across server groups, reflected and blind SSRF through attacker-controlled server URLs, non-admin creation of stdio server configurations that spawn arbitrary commands, IPv6 transition-address SSRF bypasses, and cross-tenant tool invocation against other users' MCP servers.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary NVD records with GitHub Security Advisory and release references
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: MCPHub versions before 0.12.13, 0.12.15, 1.0.29, 1.0.30, 1.0.31, or 1.0.32 depending on CVE
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: A central MCP routing hub becomes an authority multiplier: weak tenant isolation, prompt/resource integrity, process spawning, and egress filters can convert one authenticated account or bearer key into broad tool, data, and host compromise.

upstream_routing.ai_wiki: MCPHub as a broad MCP server/router entity belongs upstream if cataloged.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General MCP governance and tool workflow patterns belong upstream; this repo keeps concrete vulnerability and control implications.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence for in-window publication from NVD; several referenced GitHub advisory pages intermittently returned non-JSON/blocked responses during scripted detail collection, so per-GHSA fixed-version text should be rechecked during ingest.
follow_up_actions: Deduplicate cluster into a hub leaf plus separate high-impact leaves only where authorization, prompt shadowing, SSRF, and command spawning need independent maintenance.
Reconcile exact fixed versions from MCPHub release tags and GitHub Security Advisories.

qualifying_findings.title: Aix-DB markdown rendering stored XSS in chat and knowledge content
qualifying_findings.summary: Aix-DB through 1.2.4 rendered Markdown with raw HTML enabled into Vue v-html bindings without sanitization. Attackers could inject JavaScript through chat responses, skill descriptions, or knowledge messages that execute in users' browsers.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD CVE record with code, commit, issue, PR, and VulnCheck advisory references
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Aix-DB <=1.2.4; fixed at git commit b568a0f3b18ecead9f7d38bb78017f664d54a1a9 per NVD affected metadata
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: AI chat and knowledge surfaces are untrusted rendered-content boundaries; stored XSS can turn model, skill, or knowledge text into browser-session compromise.

upstream_routing.ai_wiki: Aix-DB as a product/entity belongs upstream if maintained.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General Markdown rendering hygiene belongs upstream only as development practice; this repo owns AI chat content trust.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence for in-window publication from NVD and linked code evidence.
follow_up_actions: Check whether any existing rendered AI-content trust leaf should absorb this finding.

qualifying_findings.summary: NVD records that improper neutralization of input used for LLM prompting in Microsoft Edge for iOS can let an unauthorized network attacker perform spoofing. The in-window qualification is the NVD lastModified timestamp; original publication predates the exact cutoff.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD CVE update with Microsoft MSRC reference
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Microsoft Edge for iOS / Chromium-based Edge before 150.0.4078.50 according to NVD affected data
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Browser-integrated LLM prompting creates a spoofing boundary where network content and prompt construction can affect user trust decisions.

qualifying_findings.title: OpenShift AI guardrails-detectors ReDoS update
qualifying_findings.summary: NVD updated CVE-2026-15154 inside the run window for a guardrails-detectors ReDoS flaw in Red Hat OpenShift AI. Crafted regular expressions sent to the public detection API can trigger catastrophic backtracking, consume a worker at 100% CPU indefinitely, and deny service to the guardrails-mediated LLM pipeline.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD CVE update with Red Hat CVE and errata references
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: guardrails-detectors before d857e059f8a2dedb5c7ea9a2c307c4cfd7983fd1; affected Red Hat OpenShift AI 2.25, 3.3, and 3.4 packages with fixed RPM versions in NVD affected data
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Guardrail services are security-critical AI runtime dependencies; a detector DoS can remove or degrade the control plane for LLM-mediated workloads.

upstream_routing.ai_wiki: OpenShift AI and TrustyAI broad entity coverage belongs upstream.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General guardrail deployment practice belongs upstream; this repo keeps detector DoS and release-gate implications.
